result.reason: The new Article XIII nominally reaches the fallback cap and includes the preferred carve-outs, but the retained provisions undermine it. They still provide that Licensee assumes all system-related liabilities and risks and that Licensor is not liable for any direct or indirect loss except direct damages caused by gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The retained absolute disclaimer of Licensor liability for IP infringement also conflicts with the new uncapped IP-infringement carve-out. Consequently, the cap and carve-outs are not genuinely mutual or effective. Drafting quality is further reduced by conflicting provisions, unnecessary reordering, run-on language, and existing errors such as “LICENSORHAS” and “gross negligence of willful misconduct.”
